purpose: Describe the desired assessment movement precisely enough for Motion Lab generation and visual verification without conflating demonstration with compensation scoring.

startPosition: knees extended but not forcefully locked
upper arms aligned beside the ears
palms facing inward toward one another/body centerline
phaseSequence: establish ear-aligned palms-in overhead standing position
controlled descent through the owner-reviewed MID geometry
hold the exact bottom pose for 0.18 seconds
controlled ascent through the same MID geometry in reverse
return to the exact overhead standing position
contactConstraints: generated bilateral leg IK owns planted-foot contact during loaded motion
Coach playback inserts grounded intermediate solve samples between named phases
no jump or heel-release phase is authored
trajectoryConstraints: pelvis descends and travels posteriorly using the existing owner-reviewed squat reference geometry
knees flex with hips and ankles rather than driving the motion alone
knees track in the same general direction as the feet
ascent mirrors the same geometry as BOTTOM -> MID -> START
each shoulder-to-elbow segment remains parallel to the current neck-to-head line so the arms stay aligned with the ears as the torso/head incline
the arms are not held vertical to the room when the head/torso angle changes
each palm faces inward throughout the movement
finish returns to the same ear-aligned palms-in overhead standing pose
rigSemanticConstraints: resolve actual loaded upper-arm and forearm bones
resolve Neck and Head as the body-relative reference line
solve shoulder-to-elbow direction parallel to Neck-to-Head after each phase torso pose is applied
resolve each hand plus middle/index/pinky landmarks
twist each hand around its long axis until its palm plane faces the head/body centerline
do not copy source-rig Euler axes to represent overhead or palm orientation
preserve the original target avatar rest pose after semantic preparation
visualAcceptanceCheckpoints: setup: upper arms sit beside ears
descent: arms travel with head/ear line instead of staying vertical to room
bottom: hands remain beside ears and palms remain inward
arms do not cross through torso, opposite shoulder, neck, or head
bilateral foot grounding between as well as at named phases

side: arms fall forward relative to ear line
assessmentObservation.importantBoundary: These are observation targets for a separate pose-analysis/scoring layer. The Motion Spec is the reference demonstration and does not diagnose causes or assign production severity thresholds.

calibrationPolicy.provisionalField: small owner-approved ear spacing and palm-plane sign refinement after semantic solve
calibrationPolicy.ownerAction: Verify the arms remain beside the ears through setup, descent and bottom, and verify both palms face inward. Use Pose Editor only for small spacing refinement; do not reintroduce fixed world-up or guessed source-rig Euler rotations.

retargetLesson.previousMistake: The first retarget copied source-rig local arm rotations; the second semantic pass improved that but defined overhead as absolute world-up.
retargetLesson.whyItFailed: An overhead squat assessment is body-relative: the head and torso incline, and the arms should remain aligned with the ears. World-up left the arms visually frozen while the head moved. Palm orientation was also omitted from the description.
retargetLesson.systemUpgrade: Support body-relative segment directions and palm-plane orientation, solved from actual target-rig geometry for every phase.

sourceNotes: Lower-body phase geometry reuses the current synthesized squat engineering reference.
Upper-arm placement is now Neck-to-Head relative rather than world-up.
Palm orientation is explicitly part of the movement definition and is solved from hand-plane landmarks.
